message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported fiscal third quarter 2026 revenue of 1.85 billion, compared with 1.35 billion a year earlier [D1]. GAAP net income was 397 million, or 2.30 per diluted share, compared with 191 million, or 1.10 per diluted share [D1]. Non-GAAP net income was 531 million, or 3.07 per share, and orders were 2.09 billion, up 56 per cent from a year earlier [D1]. Free cash flow was 403 million, compared with 291 million a year earlier, and cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled 2.62 billion as of July 31, 2026 [D1].

The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of 1,345 million, up 43 per cent from the prior year, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of 501 million, up 21 per cent [D1]. Within the Communications Solutions Group, Commercial Communications generated its first 1 billion dollar quarter, with revenue of 1.006 billion, up 56 per cent, and wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3]. Management attributed the quarter to the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, with wireline record orders more than doubling year over year [D3]. Management described the wireline mix shifting from about 80 per cent research and development and 20 per cent manufacturing toward roughly two-thirds research and development and one-third manufacturing as AI data centre build-outs scale [D3].

Fourth quarter fiscal 2026 revenue is expected in a range of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion, a midpoint representing year-over-year growth of approximately 37 per cent [D1]. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected in a range of 3.34 to 3.40, based on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1]. Management said the guidance results in fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 32 per cent and earnings per share growth of approximately 60 per cent at the midpoint [D3]. Management expects 80 per cent to 90 per cent of 100 million dollars in cost synergies to be realized on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year, with integration largely complete one quarter ahead of schedule [D3].

Shares climbed 2.6 per cent in pre-market trading after the results, with adjusted earnings per share of 3.07 against an analyst consensus of 2.48 and revenue of 1.85 billion against expectations of 1.75 billion [D2]. Fourth quarter guidance of 1.93 billion to 1.95 billion was above an analyst consensus of 1.82 billion, and the earnings per share range of 3.34 to 3.40 was above expectations of approximately 2.68 [D2]. Analysts' tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and constraints, with repeated questions on whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints limit guidance [D3]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, while cautioning that the one-time tariff impacts this year will not repeat [D3]. The mean of 12 short-term price targets is 418.42, with a standard deviation of 19.48, a lowest estimate of 390.00 and a most optimistic estimate of 452.00 [D5]. The consensus estimate for the current year rose 11 per cent over the last 30 days, with three estimates moving higher and no negative revision [D5].
